correctness.rationale: The embedded standard-library checker verified all 330 disjoint Rouché root disks for 66 degree-five Padé denominators using strict rational bounds; the real root has positive residue and strictly smaller modulus. In each case a strict rational bound puts the total competing pole contribution below 17/50 of the leading residue at n=300 and hence at every larger n. All 19,734 coefficients with 1<=n<300 are positive by independent Fraction recurrence, and the k=66,n=38 coefficient is exactly negative. Rouché plus the residue formula proves the infinite tail; enumeration alone is not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: Scardino 2026 supplies the negative witness k=66,n=38 and sufficient conditions for eventual positivity but no complete positivity theorem for the entire numerator strip 0<=k<=65. The new result establishes a globally least numerator-degree failure at fixed denominator degree five. The original Fasi-Higham conjecture is false and does not imply the lower positive range. A known all-k theorem for denominator three has a distinct hypothesis. Published/searchable priority risk is qualified; no independent audit is represented.
residual_risks: An older unpublished computation or a hard-to-index monograph may already contain this exact least-degree certificate.
The strict cutoff is for fixed denominator degree five only; no universal structure in higher m is inferred.
Same-model mathematical review and exact arithmetic replay are not independent validation.

value.rationale: The motivating false conjecture has a natural smallest counterexample question at its first explicitly disproved odd denominator order. Proving k=66 is genuinely first requires ruling out infinitely many Taylor coefficients for every smaller degree, not merely extending a finite search. The sharp lower-range classification and rational root/residue certificate identify a meaningful exact frontier in Padé matrix-exponential error analysis; no extrapolation to diagonal approximants of arbitrary degree or algorithm failure is claimed.
